svg.text: From a block down to its lanes: who holds which rows
Blue follows one path: warp 0 of the block, then quad 0 of warp 0.
it computes 64 rows (tokens); each warp takes 16
all 32 run the same instruction at the same time
A quad = 4 neighbouring lanes. Not a piece of hardware,
just how the multiply instruction hands out its results.
3. Who holds each value of warp 0's 16 × 8 multiply result
one tensor-core multiply: warp 0's 16 rows × 8 columns
Why two rows per quad: 16 × 8 = 128 values ÷ 32 lanes = 4 per lane.
Each row (8 values) goes to one quad: 4 lanes × 2 neighbouring columns.
There are 16 rows but only 8 quads, so each quad takes 2 rows: row q
and row q + 8. A row's max or sum then needs only its quad's 4 lanes
to swap values (shuffles), not the whole warp.
